statements.kind: Support for institutions and essential services
statements.scope: Security infrastructure; relief and social protection
statements.summary: Falconer backed reform and stability, visited a UK-funded army base, and highlighted education and basic-needs assistance. The embassy described £33.5 million in UK aid for 2025.
statements.condition: Reform and security are policy goals. This is not a dedicated housing-reconstruction allocation.

statements.kind: A further £13 million for humanitarian needs
statements.scope: Food, healthcare, education and basic services
statements.summary: During Chapman’s joint visit with France and Qatar, the UK announced £13 million for humanitarian services, working with Lebanese authorities and trusted partners.
statements.condition: The release calls for a lasting ceasefire; it does not state a political condition for withholding this relief.
statements.source: UK foreign ministry — June humanitarian package
statements.dateBasis: Publication date of the support announcement

statements.kind: Reform and state authority after war damage
statements.summary: After meeting Nawaf Salam, Annen urged overdue reforms and state control over force. The ministry placed Lebanon’s rebuilding alongside economic recovery and implementation of the ceasefire.
statements.condition: These are governance priorities; the release does not announce a grant or a funding-release checklist.
statements.source: German development ministry — Annen in Beirut

statements.scope: Displacement response; institutions and safe return
statements.summary: Alabali Radovan described assistance with UNICEF and UNDP alongside support for government reforms. She said displaced people need a reliable ceasefire to return home.
statements.condition: A ceasefire is described as necessary for return, not as a stated condition for releasing a reconstruction grant.
statements.source: German development ministry — June Lebanon visit

statements.kind: €15 million for relief and agricultural recovery
statements.scope: Emergency response; livelihoods in southern Lebanon
statements.summary: Tajani announced €15 million for displaced people and communities, including agricultural recovery with FAO and civil-society projects. The release notes particular attention to Christian communities within support for all communities.
statements.condition: The package is for relief and recovery; it is not wholly a housing-reconstruction fund. No political prerequisite is specified.
statements.source: Italian foreign ministry — development cooperation committee

statements.kind: A demand for compensation, not a Turkish funding pledge
statements.scope: War damage, compensation and ceasefire compliance
statements.summary: At his press conference with Najib Mikati, Erdoğan called for international pressure on Israel to comply with the ceasefire and compensate for damage caused in Lebanon.
statements.condition: This is a compensation demand. The cited passage does not commit Turkish reconstruction funding.
statements.source: Turkish presidency communications directorate — Erdoğan and Mikati

statements.kind: Mine clearance enables safe land use
statements.scope: Legacy conflict damage; land and infrastructure access
statements.summary: At the Mechref handover, Magoshi linked Japanese-funded mine clearance to safe land access and recovery. The embassy reported about 34,500 m² cleared near a university and water reservoir.
statements.condition: The project addresses a civil-war legacy; it should not be counted as clearance of new 2024–2026 war damage.
statements.access: Official English and Arabic PDF text read
statements.dateBasis: Ceremony on 30 September; embassy release dated 6 October 2025

statements.summary: Magoshi signed grant notes for ¥425 million, approximately US$3 million, to supply angiography equipment to Baabda Governmental Hospital. He emphasized equitable access to healthcare.
statements.condition: This is a targeted health grant, not a nationwide reconstruction pledge or confirmation of completed delivery.

statements.kind: Support for rebuilding under the new authorities
statements.summary: Welcoming Nawaf Salam’s designation, Spain said it would work with the emerging Lebanese authorities to support reconstruction, prosperity and regional stability.
statements.condition: A political commitment; no amount, payment schedule or explicit aid-release condition is stated.
statements.access: Official indexed text read; direct page opening failed

statements.kind: A programme linking relief and longer-term recovery
statements.summary: The Lebanon programme links emergency aid with education, water management, jobs and public institutions, working through local authorities and development partners.
statements.condition: Programme priorities are not a reconstruction funding condition. This page announces no new nationwide rebuilding total.
statements.source: Swiss foreign ministry — Lebanon cooperation programme
statements.dateBasis: Page publication date; programme activities span multiple years

statements.kind: NOK 30 million in additional emergency aid
statements.scope: Shelter, healthcare, cash support and protection
statements.summary: Aukrust announced NOK 30 million in additional humanitarian aid through UN funds and WFP, and said rebuilding destroyed infrastructure would take years.
statements.condition: The amount is humanitarian relief, not a reconstruction fund. The minister calls for civilian protection and unhindered aid access.
statements.source: Norwegian foreign ministry — additional Lebanon aid

statements.kind: C$29.7 million for urgent civilian needs
statements.summary: Joly announced C$29.7 million for food, healthcare, shelter and clean water. Canada said its funding follows needs identified in UN and Red Cross appeals.
statements.condition: This is humanitarian funding. Calls to respect the ceasefire are not presented as a reconstruction grant-release condition.
statements.source: Global Affairs Canada — Lebanon humanitarian funding

statements.summary: Dousa announced additional support, bringing targeted Swedish humanitarian assistance for 2026 to SEK 135 million.
statements.condition: Humanitarian assistance through partners; not a housing-reconstruction allocation.

statements.scope: South Lebanon and Bekaa local economies
statements.summary: Vivike stressed Lebanese leadership and coordination at the joint programme launch.
statements.condition: The €32 million is the combined programme, not Denmark’s contribution alone.
statements.source: Prime Minister’s Office — joint programme launch

statements.summary: Magro highlighted public institutions, agriculture and youth as part of the joint €32 million recovery programme.
statements.condition: Longer-term recovery depends on conditions allowing implementation; no payment is confirmed here.
statements.source: Prime Minister’s Office — joint programme launch
